t.E1105.agn: In 2023 EFSA stated that lysozyme obtained from egg did not raise a safety concern under the conditions of use, but that residual amounts in treated beer, cheese and wine may cause allergic reactions in sensitive people. In 2011 EFSA had also concluded that wines treated with lysozyme may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people with egg allergy.
t.E1105.eff.0.a: Even at residual amounts in beer, cheese and wine
t.E1105.eff.0.t: Because it is obtained from egg, it may cause an allergic reaction; in the EU it is indicated on the label as an egg allergen
t.E1105.eval: Obtained from egg white (important for people with egg allergy).
t.E1105.prod: An enzyme obtained from hen's egg white.
t.E1105.pw.0: Obtained from egg white; according to EFSA, its residues may cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to egg.
t.E1105.regx.0: No safety concern under the conditions of use, apart from the possibility of allergic reactions in sensitive people.
t.E1105.regx.1: Wines treated with lysozyme may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.
t.E1105.regx.2: Quantum satis in ripened cheese and ripened cheese products.
t.E1105.regx.3: Ingredients obtained from egg and present in the final product must be emphasised in the list of ingredients.
t.E1105.summary: An enzyme obtained from egg white. It prevents the growth of unwanted bacteria in some cheeses.
t.E1105.what: An enzyme obtained from hen's egg white that breaks down the cell walls of some bacteria and is used as a preservative in cheese.
